usageNotes: Use this to inspect a specific API token's metadata — expiry, privilege-separation flag, and comment — without revealing the token secret itself (the secret is only returned at creation time). A user can read their own tokens; reading another user's tokens requires the User.Modify privilege on the realm or a parent path. Useful when auditing token expiration or confirming whether a token runs with full user privileges or a restricted ACL (privsep).

examples.summary: Read the 'automation' token for a local admin user

tips: The token secret is never returned by this endpoint — it is only shown once, at creation (post_access_users_userid_token_tokenid). Store it securely at that time.
privsep=true (the default) means the token's effective permissions are the intersection of its ACLs and the owner's ACLs — it cannot exceed the user's own rights.
An expire value of 0 means the token never expires; check this when auditing long-lived service accounts.
tokenid must start with a letter and may contain letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores — validate before calling if building the ID programmatically.
